title: Find the largest item
prompt: Write the body of Largest<T>(List<T> items, T fallback), where T is limited to types that implement IComparable<T>. Return the largest item in the list, or the fallback when the list is empty. The fallback is used only for an empty list. It never competes with the items.
hints: With the items -5 and -2 and a fallback of 0, what must the result be?
Start from the first item, not from the fallback, and compare the rest against the best so far.
Return fallback for an empty list. Otherwise keep a best item and replace it whenever item.CompareTo(best) is greater than 0.
checkLabels: The largest of 3, 9 and 4 must be 9.
The largest of "b", "c" and "a" must be "c".
An empty list must give the fallback.
A list with one item must give that item.
The largest of -5 and -2 must be -2, whatever the fallback is.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Starts from the fallback, so it competes with the items.
Reads the comparison the wrong way round and finds the smallest.

feedback: Try a list of negative numbers with a fallback of 0. Check where your best value starts and which way the comparison points.
